cve_summary: inffast.c in zlib 1.2.8 might allow context-dependent attackers to have unspecified impact by leveraging improper pointer arithmetic.
commit_message:
Use post-increment only in inffast.c.

An old inffast.c optimization turns out to not be optimal anymore
with modern compilers, and furthermore was not compliant with the
C standard, for which decrementing a pointer before its allocated
memory is undefined. Per the recommendation of a security audit of
the zlib code by Trail of Bits and TrustInSoft, in support of the
Mozilla Foundation, this "optimization" was removed, in order to
avoid the possibility of undefined behavior.

Summary: This code fragment implements the logic for handling distance-based copying in a decompression algorithm, likely part of a decompressor for a compressed data format.

Parameters: N/A

Returns: N/A

Logic: The code checks if a specific operation flag is set to handle distance-based copying from a previously output buffer or a sliding window. It calculates the distance to copy based on the current state and the number of bits available. If the calculated distance exceeds the maximum allowed, an error message is set, and the state is marked as bad. The code then manages the copying process, either from the output buffer or the window, depending on the distance calculated. It handles cases where the distance wraps around the window and ensures that the copying respects the available length. The copying is optimized for performance by processing multiple bytes at once when possible, and it includes conditions to handle edge cases gracefully.
